messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the SDK 2.4.1 rollout we saw a sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate for a subset of production traffic (noted from 03:10 UTC). Figured it's worth a quick thread to correlate with runtime telemetry.
raj: saw the alert. numbers?
maria: baseline before deploy ~78% prefix hit-rate for chat-short pattern. After deploy it's ~41% for the same keys. Token-level cost up ~22% on that cohort. Traces show many requests hitting the runtime cold path.
kevin: any obvious canonicalization changes in 2.4.1? I remember we normalized whitespace and stripped trailing newlines in the client.
anya: yes — SDK now applies prompt normalization: collapse multiple spaces, trim trailing whitespace, and normalize CRLF -> LF. We shipped that to reduce accidental cache fragmentation, but it could change hash behavior.
maria: counterintuitive: normalization should increase hits, not reduce them. But telemetry shows client-generated header X-RW-Cache-Key differs between old and new clients.
oliver: can you paste an example pair (old vs new header)?
maria: old header: "rw-cache-key: sha1:8fb3a2..."\nnew header: "rw-cache-key: sha1:8fb3a2...:v2" — SDK appends a short suffix to indicate normalization version. Runtime keying logic ignores suffix but the edge LB started routing by full header string for warmup probing. So warmup keys no longer match internal canonical keys.
kevin: ah — that explains it. We changed an ingress LB rule last sprint that used the raw header for routing warmup probes. If the header differs warmup won't touch the KV entry and the runtime cold-starts kernel selection which biases toward conservative kernels.
raj: other contributing factor: the SDK also starts streaming chunking earlier (sends first chunk as soon as token generated). Retries now resend with identical prompt but streaming chunk boundaries differ, and our cache keying is currently length-and-chunk-sensitive for streaming flows.
anya: snippet of problematic behavior: ```
# client send
POST /v1/generate
X-RW-Cache: opt-in
rw-cache-key: sha1:8fb3a2...:v2
body: {"prompt": "Hi\n"}
# retry (network glitch)
# same prompt but SSE chunking splits differently -> runtime computes different stream-key
```
maria: TL;DR: two changes in SDK (cache-key suffix + earlier streaming chunk flush) + a routing tweak = miss storm.
oliver: size of impact? is it isolated to one model / region?
maria: mostly gpt-small-ish chat models in us-west-2. Hit-rate drop concentrated on SDK v2.4.* clients (mobile + web). Other clients unaffected.
ci-bot: Deploy 2.4.1 rolled at 2026-02-12T03:08:23Z to prod (canary 10%).
raj: remediation options: 1) revert SDK suffix quickly, 2) change LB warmup to canonicalize header before routing, 3) make runtime ignore chunk boundaries when computing streaming cache key, 4) accept suffix in warmup matching. Which is fastest?
kevin: fastest is revert suffix — push a 2.4.2 with the suffix removed (or keep but not sent for first rollout). But server-side LB fix is also quick (single rule change) and avoids client churn.
anya: runtime change to compute streaming-key independent of chunk boundaries is non-trivial (must be atomic across streaming handshake), will take longer.
oliver: propose: immediate LB rule tweak + hotfix SDK toggle to stop emitting suffix for canary clients. Medium-term: runtime change to streaming-key canonicalization + tests.
maria: agreed. Also we should add a telemetry gate: when cache hit-rate drops >10% for a client-major-version, alert to SRE/product.
raj: action items:
- oliver: rollback LB routing to canonicalize RW header (10m) — owner oliver
- kevin: publish 2.4.2 toggling suffix flag and coordinate with web/native teams (30m)
- anya: start design doc for runtime streaming-key canonicalization (+ tests) — estimate 3d
- maria: add alert rule and dashboard panel for client-major-version hit-rate deltas — 1d
- raj: follow up once LB + SDK hotfix rolled to verify hit-rate recovers
maria: I'll attach a couple of perf traces and a small script to replay affected traffic in staging (sanitized) so we can validate fixes.
kevin: also investigate kernel selection effect: many cold requests selected "safe" kernel (attn type A) which is ~1.6x slower than optimized kernel used with warm KV. If we recover hits we should see latency drop and batch sizes improve.
anya: noted. I'll add a unit in the doc explaining kernel heuristics shift when cache miss -> cold runtime path.
oliver: deploying LB tweak now.
maria: thanks everyone, I'll watch dashboards. :eyes:
kevin: ping me if you need a rollback window for 2.4.2 release.
raj: we'll reconvene in 30m to confirm metrics.
